title: Goroutines, channels and select
summary: Start concurrent work, communicate with channels, wait with WaitGroup and time out with select.
hints: `Generate`: make an unbuffered channel `ch := make(chan int)`, start `go func() { defer close(ch); for _, n := range nums { ch <- n } }()`, and return `ch` straight away. The goroutine does the sending while the caller receives. Closing is what lets the receiver's `range` loop end.

`Collect`: `for v := range ch { out = append(out, v) }`. `ParallelSum`: split the work into `parts` chunks, give each goroutine its own slot in a `sums := make([]int, parts)` slice, and wait with a `sync.WaitGroup` (`wg.Add(1)` before `go`, `defer wg.Done()` inside, `wg.Wait()` after). Distinct slots mean no two goroutines write the same memory, so no lock is needed (the race detector would tell you otherwise).

`FirstOf` uses `select`: `select { case v := <-a: return v, true; case v := <-b: return v, true; case <-time.After(timeout): return "", false }`. A `select` waits until one of its cases can proceed and runs that one.
